q: Take a green-screen shot all the way to a clean composite.
a: 1. Background on Video 1, green-screen clip on Video 2; apply Ultra Key (`effects.apply`, `ultra_key`) and set Key Color with the eyedropper on a mid-green part of the backdrop; Setting: Default first. 2. Output ▸ Alpha Channel to check the matte: speckles in the background → raise Tolerance or Transparency; holes in the person → lower Tolerance or raise Pedestal; then back to Composite. 3. Clean up: a small Choke (5–20) for a green outline, Soften for the edge, Spill Suppression for green on skin and hair, then Color Correction so the foreground sits in the new background.

q: I keyed one take perfectly; how do I reuse that on the other takes?
a: 1. Finish the key on one clip (Ultra Key with its key colour, setting, choke, soften and spill). 2. Select it and Save Preset… (`presets.save`) with a name, then apply it to the other takes from Effects ▸ Presets or `presets.apply`. Check each take's matte with Output ▸ Alpha Channel, since lighting can differ between takes.

q: Record a voice-over and get it sounding decent fast.
a: 1. Choose the microphone and input in Voice-Over Record Settings (`audio.voiceover.settings`), park the playhead and click record in the track header (`audio.voiceover.start`); the countdown beeps lead in, and the recording lands on the track as a mono WAV. 2. Select the clip and Clean Up Voice (`audio.cleanupVoice`): it measures the clip and sets Reduce Rumble, Voice Isolation (or Reduce Noise), DeEss, Dynamics and loudness at −14 LUFS under −1 dBTP; then tune by ear.
